newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas trades in discount.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas - Mogas trades in discount.

text.p: The gasoline market shrugged off crude's gains as ample supplies continued to bear down, with prompt cargoes being traded in the negative, traders said on Friday.
A U.S. major sold 80,000 barrels of 92-octane unleaded gasoline lifting April 24-26 to a European major at a discount of 85 cents per barrel to Singapore spot quotes, fob Singapore.
On a fixed price basis, two European majors offered 97-octane and 95-octane at $26.10 per barrel and $25.60 respectively, for cargoes lifting end April/early May, but buyers failed to emerge.
On Thursday, 97-octane cargo was offered down to a low of $26.30 per barrel.
Traders said regional demand was still very thin with only some potential outlet into Japan for reformate.
Naphtha swaps edged up slightly with crude with May swaps last quoted at $21.50/$21.60 per barrel, up 15 cents from Thursday.
